Cybersecurity Basics Every Irish SME Should Review

Published June 7, 2026

Small businesses do not always need complex security programmes first. They need practical checks around access, email, backups and websites.

Start with practical risk reduction

Small businesses do not always need a complex security programme first. They usually need clear control over access, safer logins, better backups, stronger email protection and a more secure website environment.

Review who has access

One of the most common risks is poor account control. Businesses should know who has admin access to the website, hosting, business email, analytics, domains, cloud tools and payment systems. Old users and shared passwords should be removed or replaced.

Email and website security matter most

Phishing, weak passwords, missing multi-factor authentication and out-of-date plugins are all common risk areas. A simple review of these basics can prevent many avoidable incidents.

Backups and recovery should be realistic

Backups only matter if they can actually be restored. Key business systems, files and websites should have backup arrangements that are tested and understood, not just assumed to be working.

The practical outcome

The aim is not fear. The aim is to reduce avoidable risk and give the business a clear list of what should be fixed first.
